newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-PRODIGIES PAST AND PRESENT VIE FOR OPEN TITLE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-PRODIGIES PAST AND PRESENT VIE FOR OPEN TITLE.

text.p: Swiss teenager Martina Hingis and a former teen prodigy, American Jennifer Capriati, prepared on Tuesday to open their Australian Open campaigns as the second day of play began at Melbourne Park.

Fourth seed Hingis, at 16 years of age the heir apparent to Steffi Graf's world number one crown, was to meet German Barbara Rittner at centre court at Melbourne Park while Capriati starts her first Open here since 1993 against American Jolene Watanabe.
Before they took the court, fifth women's seed and 1996 finalist Anke Huber got off to a dismal start against American Amy Frazier, losing the first set 6-0.

Graf is virtually unbackable to win her fifth Australian Open title, but Hingis is increasingly popular with the pundits with the draw favouring a final showdown between the two biggest names left in an injury-scarred tournament.
Hingis, who has beaten both Graf and the injured world number two and 1996 Australian Open champion Monica Seles over the past year, beat Rittner in two sets in Hamburg last year.

Capriati, on the second comeback of her career since teenage burn-out forced her to quit the tour after the 1993 U.S. Open, lost to Hingis in the final of last week's Sydney International but she too is climbing rapidly back up the rankings.
In her last appearance here four years ago, the then 16-year-old American reached the quarter-finals.

The men's draw has also lost some of the tour's best players, mainly due to injury but also thanks to unseeded Spaniard Carlos Moya who dumped defending champion Boris Becker out of the tournament on Monday.

Undisputed men's favourite Pete Sampras now looks to have an almost clear run to his second Australian Open title and Romanian qualifier Dinu Pescariu was not expected to detain him on centre court on Tuesday.

The 26-year-old American ended 1996 on a high note by winning the ATP Tour world championship in Hanover and was again in excellent form at the start of this year reaching the final of the Colonial Classic exhibition event on Saturday.
Sampras and his 169th-ranked opponent have never played each other, partly because the Romanian has only qualified for one other grand slam event -- the French Open in 1991.
Big-serving Croat Goran Ivanisevic, the third seed who is struggling for form, was to meet Australian wildcard Ben Ellwood.
Double Australian Open champion Jim Courier kicks off his tournament against Sjeng Schalken of the Netherlands.
